AI adoption is spreading far beyond tech:

80.6% of US technology and media businesses now have paid AI subscriptions, the highest percentage on record.

Finance and insurance companies follow at 73.1%, up from ~60.0% in December 2025.

Meanwhile, 60.4% of US manufacturing firms are paying for AI subscriptions, their highest proportion on record and the 3rd-highest among major sectors.

This percentage has nearly doubled since the start of 2025.

Over the same period, the proportion of retail companies paying for AI subscriptions has risen +20 percentage points, to a record 49%.

Non-tech firms are now quickly adopting AI.

The US services sector is sending mixed signals:

ISM Services PMI rose +1.3 points in August, to 55.4, its 2nd-highest reading since October 2024.

12 industries reported growth, including mining, real estate, and accommodation and food services, while 5 industries saw contraction.

The increase was driven by new orders, which surged +3.7 points, to 60.9, the highest level since February 2023 and significantly above the 56.6-point average since 1997.

Meanwhile, prices paid jumped +2.3 points, to 72.6, their highest since July 2022.

At the same time, the employment index came in at 47.8, remaining in contraction for the 2nd consecutive month and in 5 of the last 6 months.

The services sector is growing, but pricing pressures are building.

Emerging market bond spreads sit near 200 basis points, close to the lowest in a generation.

In the 1998 Asian crisis, investors demanded over 1,500 basis points of extra yield to hold EM sovereign debt ($EMB). Today they take about 200, even as developed-market bonds sell off and 30-year yields hit new highs.

Either emerging markets have truly de-risked, or the reach for yield has crushed the premium for real risk. At 200 basis points, there is almost no cushion left if that bet is wrong.
